/work/karama.description: Lumen Field Titles — cut, graded and delivered by Anamorph™.
h3: A film-grade editing and motion studio cutting reels, campaigns and title work for creatives and brands.
p: Open titles for a documentary series about builders. Patient work — it deserved a patient open.
Fifty-two seconds, eleven cards, one typeface. The pacing borrows from print: hold, breathe, turn the page. Nothing moves faster than it has to.
Print stock, not screen. Soft highlights and a paper-white base so the type feels set, not rendered.
The open ran unchanged across all eight episodes. The network asked who cut it.

/work/citadel.title: Citadel — Anamorph™
/work/citadel.description: Nomad Stays Campaign — cut, graded and delivered by Anamorph™.
h3: A film-grade editing and motion studio cutting reels, campaigns and title work for creatives and brands.
p: Nomad Stays wanted the feeling of arriving somewhere new and unpacking like you own it. Twelve locations, one film, no voiceover.
The rhythm is built on doors opening — every location enters mid-motion, nothing establishes. The master runs under two minutes; each cutdown opens on a different city.
Every city graded to the same warm base, so twelve locations read as one brand. No teal, no postcard look.
Four cutdowns carried the campaign across three markets. The hero film doubled the previous campaign’s completion rate.

/work/flora.title: Flora — Anamorph™
/work/flora.description: Signal Product Reveal — cut, graded and delivered by Anamorph™.
h3: A film-grade editing and motion studio cutting reels, campaigns and title work for creatives and brands.
p: Signal’s reveal had one rule: show the product before you explain it. Hardware this small is easy to oversell.
The film opens on the device at true scale and earns every zoom after it. Three loops shipped alongside — the store page runs the twelve-second one.
Graded like hardware photography, deep neutrals and a single specular pass, so renders and live plates match.
The reveal held the store page for a full quarter. The twelve-second loop outperformed every static frame.

/privacy.title: Privacy Policy — Anamorph™
/privacy.description: What gets collected, what doesn’t, and where it goes.
h3: A film-grade editing and motion studio cutting reels, campaigns and title work for creatives and brands.
p: What gets collected, what doesn’t, and where it goes. The short cut.
When you send the booking form, Noah receives the details you type: your name, your email and whatever you share about the project. Nothing more is gathered behind the scenes.
Your details are used to reply to your enquiry and to scope the work. They are never sold, rented or added to a mailing list you didn’t ask for.
Analytics here are light and anonymous: page views and rough location, enough to see which cuts hold attention. No advertising trackers, no fingerprinting.
The site is hosted on Framer and video is streamed from Vimeo. Both may set the minimum cookies needed to serve their content. Their policies apply to their pipes.
Ask at any time to see, correct or delete what’s held about you. One email is enough.
Questions about privacy go straight to the editor’s desk. Replies within a working day.

/work/meridian.title: Meridian — Anamorph™
/work/meridian.description: Identity & Launch Film — cut, graded and delivered by Anamorph™.
h3: A film-grade editing and motion studio cutting reels, campaigns and title work for creatives and brands.
p: A new identity needed a film that could carry it — sixty days from first board to launch, and a name the market hadn’t heard yet.
We cut to the grade, not around it. Two-frame holds on the wordmark, hard cuts on the beat, nothing that lingers. The launch version ran 02:14; the boardroom sat through it twice.
Lifted blacks and one warm accent pulled from the wordmark. The whole film sits inside the brand palette before the logo ever appears.
The film opened the launch event and ran paid for six weeks. Average watch time held above ninety per cent.
